THE PARK IS UPHELD AS A SOURCE CAP AND REFUTED AS A STATEMENT THAT THE RESIDUAL IS UNREACHABLE. attempt.parked.mbrendertext-color-tiebreak.20260901.v4 reached its fourth version screening source-axis levers (the run-19 volatile-binding law, an interference lever) against 'an r0<->r3 colour tie-break at +0x108..+0x130'. The window shipped here is EXACTLY [0x108,0x130) -- the park had localised the mechanism perfectly and mis-classified only its REACHABILITY. It is not a colour choice source can steer: it is a schedule difference whose displacement is caused by the recolor, so no source form addresses it and no PRE permutation reaches it either (the pre placement was enumerated and refuses).

MECHANISM. The stage runs LAST. The recolor aims at the intermediate image obtained by applying the permutation's INVERSE to the target (unpermute_target_windows), which restores position correspondence so the UNCHANGED verify_consistent_recolor adjudicates a genuine renaming and is never asked to reason about a reordering; the permutation then carries the intermediate to the target. The window is relocation-free in both objects, which that stage requires and refuses without.

TRIAGE NOTE. A park that names an OFFSET RANGE is far more valuable than one that names a register pair: this close cost one search because the park had already told me where to look. Parks in the colour/tie-break family should record the byte range as a matter of course, and should be re-screened against the post-recolor placement before any further source version is attempted.
